free_tier.stated: Pump Priming is always open and awards a maximum of 4,000 CU for six months through a light-touch form sent to the service desk, with a decision expected in under two weeks; the Driving Test awards 800 CU including GPU nodes to new users, and Director's Time is always open but restricted to University of Edinburgh researchers.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The Driving Test gets a new user onto the GPU nodes for 800 CU, and Pump Priming then carries the same code to 4,000 CU, so the two compose into a single ramp inside one national system.

limits.value: Pump Priming is open only to researchers within the EPSRC remit, meaning eligibility for UKRI EPSRC funding and a UK research organisation, so the form is light but the applicant still needs a UK institutional base.

'We expect decisions to be made in less than 2 weeks (and usually much sooner). A maximum of 4000 CU for 6 months are currently available through Pump Priming', quoted
'A small allocation (800 CU) for new ARCHER2 users to get them started using the ARCHER2 Service ... Includes access to GPU nodes', quoted

notes: The always-open, form-only structure makes this the closest UK analogue to the trial tiers found in Germany and the US, and the sub-two-week decision is faster than any peer-reviewed call. The binding term is 'EPSRC remit', which is a funding-eligibility test rather than a nationality test, but it still resolves to a UK research organisation. CU means CPU-hour equivalent on ARCHER2 and is not a GPU-hour unit, so no conversion is offered.
